title: The 7th and T jam session setup: Toby, Walter Page and Paul Jones
summary: At 7th and T the house pianist Toby, Walter Page on bass and Chester Brown on guitar played with no drums; Red Elkins taunted Paul Jones, then the best tenor in town, that Lester was coming.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Paul was playing at the Bluebird over in Virginia.
Yeah, he and Red Elkins. Red was playing with Paul at the Bluebird Inn. And Julius Pogue.
So you went up to 7th and T..
We went up to 7th and T. Who was playing? Toby. They had a piano around there; he was a little punk. Oh, he could play some piano! I don't know whether you know him...
You mentioned him the other day. You said he was in that place. He was the regular pianist there.
Yeah, the regular pianist. Toby.
They didn't have anybody but him.
That's all. And other guys would come up. They'd bring their basses and guitars. Very few of them brought drums. But that's all they needed. When Prez was
Phillips - 185
playing, all they had was a guitar and bass -- piano.
That night, you mentioned before that Walter Page came up there.
Yeah, that's right. Page was there. He brought his bass.
There was a guitar or not?
Yeah, Chester Brown was up there.
Chester Brown was on guitar, Walter Page was on bass, Toby was on piano.
Yes.
Anybody on drums?

No, they didn't have no drums. Anyway, Red said, "Paul, that's the cat I been tellin' you about." Paul said, "I'm ready for him." "He says he's ready for you. He's ready for all cats like you. He was ready for you when he first started playing." And Red was giving Paul... He and Paul didn't get along too good; he was giving him hell. He said, "When he first started blowin' the horn, he was ready for you." Paul said, "I'll find out tonight." Because he was supposed to be the greatest tenor player around here in Washington.
Paul Jones.
Paul Jones, yeah.
Whatever happened to him?
Oh, he quit playing. He went in the Post
Phillips - 186

Office during the war-time. Got a job in the Post Office. He had a family, you know. So he quit playing. He was a good player all right, but he wasn't no Lester Young! I remember Julius, the one I just got through talking about... Paul's tone was kind of raggedy. I don't know, looked like he was strainin' to blow. You know what I mean? He wasn't smooth. But he could play. Something like on the order of Tex Beneke.
So he played. He pulled his horn out and he started blowing. He started. Then Page come up and brought his bass. Paul started playing before Page got up there, then Page started playing the bass.
